description: Synthetic case for the Globe instrument. Every record, position, time and source here was written for the design studies and this fixture. Nothing is an observation, a real account, or a real place name. The coordinates fall on real terrain only so that the globe has something to draw under them.

interval.note: Case interval in reported local time. No UTC instant is recorded for any account.

records.label: Account A

geometry.basis: Observer position as described in the transcript: the eastern valley road near the bridge. The fixture author placed the point; the 150 m radius is the author's bound on that description.

records.notes: Reported one light moving northwest to southeast over about eight minutes. Direction and duration are testimony; no track is recorded, so none is drawn.

records.label: Account B
records.geometry_absent_reason: Position not recorded in the source.
records.notes: Heard about the sighting the next morning; could not say where they were that evening.

records.label: Account C

geometry.label: East of the ridge
geometry.basis: The account describes two lights 'east of the ridge'. The region is the fixture author's bound on that phrase. It is an area claim, not a position, and has no centre.

records.notes: Two lights, low over the eastern slope, no duration given.

records.label: Weekly article

geometry.basis: The article names only 'the valley'. The point is a gazetteer-style centroid chosen by the fixture author with a 3 km radius; it must not be read as where anything happened.

records.notes: Secondary account summarising the interviews. Not an independent source.
